Building LLM Applications

Four approaches to building an LLM-powered bot—and the architecture, retrieval and production controls around it.

Explore the slides

Choose the approach, then build the system around it

This deck compares hosted APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning and foundation-model training. It then examines orchestration, memory, function calling, retrieval pipelines, post-processing and response synthesis.

The final section connects prototypes to production through evaluation, guardrails, permissions, privacy, observability and cost management. The four options are teaching patterns rather than mutually exclusive architectures.

Four approaches at a glance

ApproachMechanismFocus
LLM APIPrompt a hosted modelGeneral tasks and prototypes
RAGRetrieve context for each questionAnswers grounded in selected business documents
Fine-tuningAdapt model weights using examplesTask behavior, tone and output formats
Foundation modelPre-train a model from scratchSpecialized requirements at substantial data and compute scale

Four Ways to Build an LLM Bot

Building LLM Apps 0 1 · F O U R O P T I O N S Four ways to build an LLM-powered bot 1 LLM API Call a hosted model with well-designed prompts KNOWLEDGE The model's public training data EFFORT AND COST 2 RAG Retrieve your latest data and add it to the prompt KNOWLEDGE Your documents, fetched per question EFFORT AND COST 3 Fine-tune Adapt a foundation model's weights with your data KNOWLEDGE Your data, built into the model EFFORT AND COST 4 Foundation model Train your own model from scratch KNOWLEDGE Your data, from the ground up EFFORT AND COST More control, more cost and more skills needed → 2

Option 1: LLM API

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 1 · F O U R O P T I O N S Option 1: LLM API bot Knowledge: the model's universal, public training data User Chatbot Prompt management and response formation LLM API The chatbot sends well-designed prompts to a hosted model through its API and formats the reply. No company data is involved. HOW IT WORKS Use an LLM API and universal data. Prompts and templates do all the work. BEST FOR Drafting, summarizing, general questions, fast prototypes. WATCH OUT Knows nothing about your business or events after its training cutoff. 3

Slide 4 of 17

Option 2: RAG with Your Data

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 1 · F O U R O P T I O N S Option 2: RAG bot with your data Knowledge: your latest data, retrieved for each question User Chatbot Prompt with context, management and formation LLM API Vector DB: your latest data context Your documents are indexed in a vector database. For each question, the relevant passages are retrieved and added to the prompt. HOW IT WORKS Use an LLM API with your latest data, supplied as context in the prompt. BEST FOR Company knowledge, policies, product and support questions; answers with citations. WATCH OUT Answers are only as good as retrieval. Keep the index current and access-controlled. 4

Slide 5 of 17

Option 3: Fine-Tuning

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 1 · F O U R O P T I O N S Option 3: Fine-tuned bot with your data Knowledge: your data in the model's weights, plus your latest data via retrieval User Chatbot Prompt with context, management and formation Fine-tuned model Vector DB: your latest data context Foundation LLM + your data fine-tune A foundation model is further trained on your examples. Retrieval still supplies facts that change. HOW IT WORKS Use your data to fine-tune a foundation model, and your latest data through a vector DB. BEST FOR Consistent tone and format, domain terminology, specialized tasks such as classification or extraction. WATCH OUT Needs quality training data, evaluation and retraining. Fine-tuning teaches behaviour better than facts. 5

Slide 6 of 17

Option 4: Your Own Foundation Model

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 1 · F O U R O P T I O N S Option 4: Your own foundation model Knowledge: a model pre-trained on your data, plus your latest data via retrieval User Chatbot Prompt with context, management and formation Your foundation model Vector DB: your latest data context Your data at large scale pre-train The model is trained from scratch on a very large corpus that includes your data. Retrieval still supplies the latest facts. HOW IT WORKS Pre-train a foundation model on your data, then serve it with retrieval for fresh facts. BEST FOR Organizations with unique data at very large scale, or strict sovereignty and control needs. WATCH OUT Very high cost in data, compute and specialist skills. Rarely justified when options 1–3 work. 6

Choosing an Approach

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 1 · F O U R O P T I O N S Choosing an option Option How your data is used Freshness Cost and effort Best for 1 LLM API Not used; prompts only Training cutoff Low General tasks, prototypes 2 RAG Retrieved at question time As fresh as the index Medium Company knowledge and support 3 Fine-tune Built into model weights, plus RAG Last training run, plus RAG Medium–high Tone, format, specialized tasks 4 Foundation Pre-training from scratch, plus RAG Last training run, plus RAG Very high Unique data at large scale Start with option 1 or 2. Add fine-tuning when prompts and retrieval can't get the behaviour right. Training your own foundation model is rarely justified. 7

Five Building Blocks

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 2 · A R C H I T E C T U R E Five building blocks of every LLM app All large language models share the same interaction model: you prompt the model and get back a response. Everything else is built around that loop. Prompt and response Send a prompt, get a response. The core of every LLM app. Prompt templates Reuse common prompt parts, with parameters for user input and context. Memory The model keeps no state between calls. Store history and facts outside and add them back. Function calling Tell the model which functions exist and how to call them, so it can reach external systems. Planning Break complex tasks into steps: divide and conquer, chain-of-thought reasoning, agents. 9

Function Calling Step by Step

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 2 · A R C H I T E C T U R E Function calling, step by step 1 User asks “Where is my order A-1042?” 2 App sends prompt + tool list Each tool has a name, description and parameter schema 3 Model chooses a tool Returns a structured call instead of text 4 App runs the function Calls your order system with the arguments 5 Result goes back to the model The app adds the JSON result to the conversation 6 Model answers the user Uses the real data, not a guess TOOL DEFINITION (STEP 2) {"name": "get_order_status", "parameters": {"order_id": "string"}} MODEL'S CALL (STEP 3) {"tool": "get_order_status", "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042"}} FUNCTION RESULT (STEP 5) {"status": "shipped", "eta": "Nov 12"} ANSWER (STEP 6) Your order A-1042 has shipped and should arrive on Nov 12. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard for connecting models to tools and data, now under the Linux Foundation. 10

Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 3 · R A G RAG: retrieval-augmented generation RAG is an AI framework that retrieves facts from an external knowledge base to ground a large language model's answers. Up-to-date information Answers use your latest documents, not the model's training cutoff. Accurate for the task The model reasons over the passages that matter for this question. Visible sources Users can see which documents the answer came from. When to use RAG • You need the latest information • Answers must be compliant and come from approved sources • The task is specific to your business Less useful for General knowledge, creative writing, and tasks where the model's style matters more than facts. 11

Inside the RAG Retriever

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 3 · R A G Inside the RAG retriever Knowledge base Retriever method Node post-processor Response synthesizer Your documents, FAQs, tables and policies, kept current Finds candidate chunks. Index types: • Vector: similar meaning • Keyword table: exact terms • Summary: whole documents • Tree: summaries of summaries • Knowledge graph: entities and links Cleans up and reorders what was found: • Handle similar items • Handle keywords • Handle the middle section • Re-rank • Handle recency Turns the chunks into an answer: • Compact • Refine • Tree summarize • Format: bullets, tree, table, JSON RAG: grounding AI in truth. AI that taps into your knowledge and uses LLM reasoning. 13

Slide 14 of 17

Node Post-Processing

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 3 · R A G Why use a node post-processor Problem What happens Post-processor fix Lost in the middle Answers at the beginning or end of a long document are used; the middle is ignored Reorder chunks so the most relevant sit at the start and end Too many similar chunks Many near-identical articles crowd out other useful context Remove duplicates; set a similarity cutoff Unwanted keywords Some terms must be excluded, or offensive and sensitive words ignored Keyword filter: required and excluded terms Compliance wording Regulated outputs must use only approved language Keep only approved sources and terms Weak ranking The first similarity search puts the best chunk too low Re-rank with a cross-encoder or LLM reranker Stale content Old versions outrank current ones Recency filter or time-weighted scoring 14
Back to slide navigation

Slide 15 of 17

Response Formation

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 3 · R A G Response formation: turning chunks into answers Compact Pack as many chunks as fit into each call, then refine across calls. Fewer LLM calls; the usual default. Refine Answer from the first chunk, then improve the answer with each next chunk. Thorough but slower. Tree summarize Summarize groups of chunks, then summarize the summaries. Good for long or many documents. Format the output Convert to bullet points, a tree structure, a table or JSON for the channel. Others: accumulate (a separate answer from each chunk, then combined) and simple summarize (one call, if everything fits). 15

From Prototype to Production

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Building LLM Apps 0 4 · P R O D U C T I O N From prototype to production Evaluate A golden set of real questions, run on every change to model, prompt or index. Guardrails Check inputs and outputs: groundedness, safety, topic limits. Security Defend against prompt injection; enforce user permissions on retrieval and tools. Privacy Mask personal data in prompts, logs and indexes; set retention. Cost and latency Cache answers, route easy questions to smaller models, limit context. Observability Trace every step: prompt, retrieved chunks, tool calls, response, feedback. 16

Key Takeaways

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Key takeaways 1 Pick the simplest option that works: API, then RAG, then fine-tuning. 2 Every LLM app is prompts, templates, memory, tools and planning. 3 RAG keeps answers current and shows sources; retrieval quality decides answer quality. 4 Post-processors and response modes are where good RAG becomes great RAG. 5 Plan for evaluation, guardrails, privacy and cost before launch. 17

Frequently asked questions

What are the four approaches in this presentation?

The deck compares calling an LLM API, adding retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning a foundation model, and training a foundation model from scratch.

How do RAG and fine-tuning differ?

RAG supplies retrieved information at query time. Fine-tuning changes model weights using training examples, often to improve behavior, format or specialized task performance. The approaches can be combined.

What happens during function calling?

The application supplies tool definitions, the model requests a structured call, and the application executes the authorized function. The result is returned to the model so it can answer using the retrieved system data.

What does the RAG pipeline include?

The slides separate indexing from answering: documents are chunked, embedded and stored; queries retrieve context, post-process candidates and synthesize an answer with sources.

Does RAG guarantee correct or compliant answers?

No. Retrieval quality, document freshness, permissions and response checks all matter. Approved sources and citations support review but do not alone establish correctness or compliance.
